beats.text: The less you know, the more you overrate yourself.
beats.note: The 1999 paper by Justin Kruger and David Dunning ran four studies on humour, logical reasoning and grammar.

beats.context: Cornell undergraduates rated 30 jokes in the first study.

beats.note: In the first study they placed themselves at the 58th. The abstract's summary across the paper puts it at the 62nd.

beats.text: The peak called Mount Stupid is not in the paper.
beats.note: Its Figure 1 plots perceived ability against actual test score, grouped by quartile.

beats.text: Some researchers call it mostly a statistical artefact.
beats.note: One paper by Gignac and Zajenkowski carries that title, and the critique leans on regression to the mean.

beats.text: The data is in the paper. The mountain is not.

beats.line: Check the chart against the paper.
